def fruit_distribution(s, n):

        if i.isdigit():
            lis.append(int(i))
    return n - sum(lis)

# Unit test for function fruit_distribution
def test_fruit_distribution():
    # Basic case with two counts
    assert fruit_distribution("5 apples and 6 oranges", 19) == 8
    assert fruit_distribution("5 apples and 6 oranges", 21) == 10

    # Zero counts
    assert fruit_distribution("0 apples and 1 oranges", 3) == 2
    assert fruit_distribution("0 apples and 0 oranges", 5) == 5

    # Equal distribution, result is zero
    assert fruit_distribution("1 apples and 1 oranges", 2) == 0

    # Multi-digit numbers
    assert fruit_distribution("10 apples and 20 oranges", 100) == 70
    assert fruit_distribution("100 apples and 200 oranges", 350) == 50

    # No digits in string
    assert fruit_distribution("apples and oranges", 7) == 7

    # Only digits in string
    assert fruit_distribution("3 4", 10) == 3

    # Single digit count
